description: §6.7.1a — the reactive-assign binding of a `:>` recovery arm, `@status = risky() !{ | ::Boom :> "caught" }`, inside an `on mount { }` body. On baseline bc51b610 this fails LOUD with E-CODEGEN-INVALID-LOGIC (the string rewriter cannot lower `!{}`), same as the `let`/bare forms of a `:>` arm. Post-fix the mount body routes through the real statement codegen, the recovery arm runs, and "caught" (not the raw {__scrml_error} envelope) lands in @status. No input — the boot/mount shape. (The distinct SILENT-DROP behavior — assign + a `-> { }` BLOCK arm — is pinned separately by onmount-error-arm-assign-drop-rt.)
rationale: §6.7.1a sugar-equivalence — the `@cell = call() !{...}` recovery-into-cell contract (§19.4.3) must hold inside `on mount` exactly as inside a `function`. risky() fails Boom; the ::Boom recovery arm produces "caught", the value written to @status. Pre-fix this exact case fails E-CODEGEN-INVALID-LOGIC (loud), not a silent miscompile — the pin asserts it now lowers and the recovered value reaches the cell.
